image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Precast concrete cylindrical litter bin with a thick wall and a rounded top rim, a shallow domed grey lid with a side throw-in opening, an exposed-aggregate pebble-dash outer surface Materials: grey concrete with exposed brown and white pebble aggregate, moss and dark water staining at the base, chipped rim.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92 -- the five layers mean 0.912 and the three critical features 0.923. 1,638/2,000 triangles, 2/2 draw calls, 2/2 materials, 2/4 unique geometries, two 512 px canvases at 2.0 MB.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope 0.44 x 0.85 x 0.44 m AT THE LID FLANGE (barrel 0.41), re-derived from a full plate solve: camera elevation 7.03 deg off the flange ellipse, 962 px/m across and 954 px/m up, object 0.914 m in plate metres scaled by 0.930 into the declared envelope, dome cap verified by predicting the plate widths at rows 108 and 152 (235/314 px against 232/311). Band table against the PLATE (scratch/_prop/binbands.mjs, diameters, shadow rows excluded): mean |delta| 0.0119 of H over ten bands, bands 0-7 (foot, barrel, sleeve, flange; 0.25-0.85 of H) ALL within 0.0125 H.
featureReviews.notes: Bands 8-9 read +0.031/+0.023: a row scan of a perspective plate smears the flange over the +-0.030 H of its own ellipse, so the lid cannot be resolved finer than that. No Meshy proxy this round -- the first build's was cleaned with the scratch tree.

featureReviews.evidence: Sleeve r 0.2185 over 0.072-0.344 m, 13.5 mm proud (the plate's silhouette steps out 12.5 px at row 562), 20 mm splayed lead-ins. 512 px pebble canvas at 18-26 mm stones sized off the plate, each over a contact shadow at 0.70 of the mortar ground; renders #8c7757 (luma 121, sat 0.379) against the crop's #907b65 (129, 0.353). Visible at 0, 90, 180, 270.
featureReviews.notes: Seeded field, not a map of the plate's stones; the band's top edge ships straight where the plate's is ragged.

featureReviews.evidence: A REAL void, not a patch: the barrel ring over 0.487-0.625 m is an open partial cylinder sweeping 4.983 rad so the 1.30 rad arc is missing, closed by a sill wedge whose top disc is the lit shelf (3 mm proud across exactly the void's arc), a soffit wedge whose bottom disc is the ceiling, a back wall 0.10 m in and two 16 mm reveal jambs. Void rows and arc measured at x 460/500/560/600 (0.487-0.625 m, 5-79 deg). Moss as a 70-cluster field in the grime canvas plus an axis tint over the sleeve's bottom 0.07 m. Lid flange r 0.220 overhanging the barrel by 15 mm, seam undercut, proud collar, and a raised collar HOLE (bore r 0.030, rim r 0.041) at 56.5 deg off vertical where the first build had a stub.
featureReviews.notes: The chamber's 0.10 m depth is inferred: the plate's interior measures luma 3-18 everywhere, so how far back it goes is not observable.

name: Concrete Street Bin
nameTh: ถังขยะคอนกรีต
notes: The heavy precast bins in public parks, temple grounds and beachfronts, too heavy to steal. One solid casting with a loose lid: the lid is not hinged, so it ships one root pivot only, no sockets and no destruction groups. The lid is modelled seated and immovable. Cylinder collider for the round body. Declared width corrected 0.60 -> 0.44 at model time (2026-08-27). REBUILT 2026-08-31 on a full plate camera solve (elevation 7.03 deg off the lid-flange ellipse; 962 px/m across, 954 px/m up; the object stands 0.914 m in plate metres, so rows scale by 0.85/0.914 = 0.930): the 0.44 m envelope now belongs to the LID FLANGE (r 0.220) and the barrel is r 0.205, because the plate reads w/h 0.459 where a barrel filling the envelope reads 0.518. The throw-in opening is a REAL void through the barrel (0.487-0.625 m, 1.30 rad) with a lit sill, reveal jambs and a chamber 0.10 m deep, not the painted patch the first build shipped; the pipe stub is a raised collar HOLE. Fidelity 0.88 -> 0.92.
